newsitem.title: INDIA: Narayanan sworn in as Indian president.
newsitem.headline: Narayanan sworn in as Indian president.

text.p: Kocheril Raman Narayanan was sworn in on Friday as the 10th president of India, the world's most populous democracy.
Narayanan, the first member of a low Hindu caste to be India's head of state, was elected last week to succeed Shankar Dayal Sharma, whose five-year term ended on Friday.

Traditionally seen as a rubber-stamp job, the post of the president, India's constitutional head, is considered crucial following the emergence of coalition politics in which the president plays a key role in government formation.
In his inaugural speech, Narayanan, 76, denounced the spread of political corruption and urged political parties to work together in fighting poverty.
"Excessive obsession with the pursuit of pure politics has often overshadowed the social, economic and developmental needs of the people," he said after being sworn in.

"Can we not sink our differences, as we have done in the critical occasions in our history, even in the recent election of the president of the republic and devote our undivided attention... to the development of the economy and the welfare of the people?," he said.
Narayanan's candidature was backed by India's three main political groups -- the ruling United Front coalition, its vital ally the Congress party, and the main opposition Bharatiya Janata Party.
